assets.name: host filesystem outside the store root
assets.whyItMatters: the process runs as some service user; files it can read (credentials, keys, config) or write (startup scripts, authorized_keys, config consumed by other daemons) are the highest-value target reachable from this code

assets.name: stored values under the store root
assets.whyItMatters: the data the store exists to hold; callers trust reads to return what was written

assets.name: process availability
assets.whyItMatters: docs/SPEC.md:13-15 makes non-termination on malformed input an explicit requirement; a panic takes down every other client sharing the process

assets.name: cached entries
assets.whyItMatters: eviction correctness is a stated bound (docs/SPEC.md:10-12); over-eviction silently degrades every tenant of the cache, not just the requester

capabilities: supplies arbitrary request strings that reach `handle_request` — arbitrary length, arbitrary colon placement, arbitrary non-numeric fields
supplies arbitrary key strings that reach `FileStore::read`/`FileStore::write`, including `..` components, absolute paths, and nested directory paths
issues requests repeatedly and concurrently, driving cache growth and eviction
in a threaded embedder, triggers concurrent `SharedCounter::read_or_init` and `SharedCounter::remove` on the same key by interleaving requests
nonCapabilities: cannot execute code on the host directly: there is no exec, no dynamic loading, and no shell invocation anywhere in the workspace
cannot choose the store root — it is fixed by the embedder at `FileStore::new` (kvstore/src/storage.rs:14-17) and never derived from request data
cannot read or write process memory: the only `unsafe` block in the workspace is a bounds-checked 4-byte read (kvstore/src/storage.rs:42-49), and nothing else in the crate handles raw pointers
cannot influence the cache capacity, which the CLI hard-codes to 64 (kvstore-cli/src/main.rs:6)

cannot reach `FileStore` through `handle_request` at this revision — `api.rs` imports only `cache`, so filesystem threats require an embedder that calls `FileStore` with wire keys, which the crate's own doc comment invites

dataCrossing.guarantees: none: the crate documents these as untrusted wire requests, and no authentication, length bound, or shape check precedes the call
dataCrossing.validation: verb is matched against `get`/`put` with an unknown-verb fallback, but the `put` arm assumes both remaining fields exist and that the ttl field parses as u64

dataCrossing.guarantees: none: `read` is documented as receiving untrusted wire keys
types: arbitrary key strings used as path components
dataCrossing.validation: none — the key is joined to the root with no normalization, component filtering, or post-join containment check

components.description: Parses `verb:arg[:arg]` wire requests and dispatches to the cache. The declared entry point for untrusted data.
components.name: request-api

components.description: Bounded in-memory map plus FIFO eviction order, and a mutex-guarded shared counter map.
components.name: cache

components.description: Maps a caller-supplied key to a path under a root directory and reads/writes that file; also parses a magic number out of a byte buffer with unsafe code.
components.name: file-store

components.description: Constructs a 64-entry cache and feeds each argv element to `handle_request`. The only in-tree caller of the library.
components.name: cli-harness

criticality.critical: read or write of files outside the configured store root, or any path from request data to code execution on the host
criticality.high: process termination or permanent functional disablement from a single malformed or concurrent request — the spec makes non-termination an explicit guarantee, so breaking it breaks the product's contract
criticality.low: correctness and efficiency defects bounded by the cache's own contents, with no data leaving the process
criticality.medium: disclosure of host state (path existence, error text) or corruption of stored values within the root

focusPaths.reason: the key→path mapping: every untrusted key becomes a filesystem path here with no confinement check, and it holds the workspace's only unsafe block
the declared untrusted-input entry point; the `put` arm converts malformed input into panics via three unwraps in two lines
holds both the eviction arithmetic that defines the memory bound and the check-then-act counter logic that panics and poisons under concurrency

notes: No network listener exists at this revision. Severity is calibrated against the deployment the crate documents for itself — embedded behind a wire protocol, with requests and keys arriving from the network (kvstore/src/api.rs:12-15, kvstore/src/storage.rs:19, docs/SPEC.md:13-19) — not against the in-tree CLI, where the operator supplies argv and is the data owner. If this library is only ever used as the CLI uses it, TM-001 through TM-004 drop to self-inflicted bugs.

`FileStore` is not reachable from `handle_request` at this revision: `api.rs` imports only `cache`. TM-002 requires an embedder to wire wire-keys into `FileStore` directly — which is exactly what the method's doc comment anticipates, so the gap is recorded rather than dismissed.

docs/adr/adr-0001-layering.md prohibits upward imports, yet `storage.rs:3` imports `crate::api::Response` for `status_response`. That is architectural drift rather than a security threat, but it is also the mechanism by which raw `io::Error` strings reach the response type in TM-002.
The workspace has no dependencies beyond std (Cargo.toml declares only workspace members), so there is no supply-chain surface to model here.
output.summary: A Rust workspace holding a reusable key-value library (`kvstore`) and a thin CLI harness (`kvstore-cli`). The library is explicitly written to be driven by untrusted input: `handle_request` is documented as taking wire requests (kvstore/src/api.rs:12-15), `FileStore::read` is documented as receiving keys that 'arrive from the wire untrusted' (kvstore/src/storage.rs:19), and docs/SPEC.md:13-19 states requests and keys come from the network and must never terminate the process or escape the store root. No listener ships in this repository yet, so the boundary is the library's public API surface: any embedder that hands attacker-supplied strings to `handle_request` or `FileStore` crosses it. Two things are worth attacking: the host filesystem reachable through the key→path mapping, and the availability of the process, which several unwraps hand away for free.

threats.action: send `put` with a missing key (`put`), a missing ttl (`put:k`), or a non-numeric ttl (`put:k:abc`), so that `parts.next().unwrap()` or `.parse().unwrap()` unwinds

existingControls.description: the `get` arm handles a missing key by returning `Response::Error("bad request")` rather than unwrapping, and an unrecognized verb falls through to `Response::Error("unknown verb")` — the `put` arm does neither

gaps: `parts.next().unwrap().parse().unwrap()` on the ttl field — two panics in one expression (kvstore/src/api.rs:27)
threats.impact: panic on the handling thread; in a single-threaded server the whole process terminates, denying service to every other client and violating the explicit spec requirement that malformed input never terminate the process
mitigations: match the `put` arm on `(parts.next(), parts.next())` and return `Response::Error("bad request")` when either is absent
propagate the `parse::<u64>()` error into `Response::Error` instead of unwrapping
prerequisites: ability to send one request string
threats.title: Malformed `put` request panics the process

threats.action: send a key containing `..` segments (`../../etc/shadow`) or an absolute path (`/etc/cron.d/x`, `C:\...`) — `Path::join` with an absolute argument discards the root entirely, and `..` segments are never normalized away
gaps: no rejection of `..` or absolute keys before `self.root.join(key)` in `read` (kvstore/src/storage.rs:21)
no rejection before the same join in `write`, which additionally creates parent directories outside the root (kvstore/src/storage.rs:26-30)
`status_response` reflects the resulting `io::Error` text back to the caller, turning failed traversals into a filesystem-existence oracle (kvstore/src/storage.rs:34-39)
threats.impact: read of any file the process user can read, and write of attacker-chosen bytes to any path the process user can write; `write` even calls `create_dir_all` on the escaped parent, so it creates the directory tree it needs. An attacker-controlled write into a location another daemon executes converts this into code execution indirectly. Directly violates the store-confinement requirement in docs/SPEC.md:16-17
impactedAssets: host filesystem outside the store root
stored values under the store root
mitigations: reject keys that are absolute or contain any non-normal path component before joining
canonicalize the joined path and verify it still starts with the canonicalized root, failing closed when canonicalization errors
return a generic error from `status_response` rather than the raw `io::Error` string
prerequisites: an embedder that passes wire-supplied keys to `FileStore::read` or `FileStore::write`, which the method's own doc comment describes as the expected usage
threats.title: Key is joined to the store root without confinement, escaping it

threats.action: race `remove(k)` against `read_or_init(k)` so the entry disappears between the `contains_key` check and the `get` — the lock is acquired and released three separate times in one logical operation

existingControls.description: the counter map is guarded by a `Mutex`, so no data race occurs — the flaw is in the check-then-act sequencing, not in memory safety

gaps: `contains_key`, `get`, and `insert` each take and drop the lock independently, so the check does not hold across the act (kvstore/src/cache.rs:76-83)
threats.impact: `.unwrap()` on the now-`None` `get` panics; because the panic occurs while the mutex is held, the mutex is poisoned and every subsequent `.lock().unwrap()` in `read_or_init` and `remove` panics too, permanently disabling counters for the process lifetime. Violates the concurrent-counter correctness requirement in docs/SPEC.md:18-19
mitigations: take the lock once into a local guard and use the entry API: `*guard.entry(key.to_string()).or_insert(0)`
never `.unwrap()` a `get` whose presence was established under a different lock acquisition
prerequisites: `remove` and `read_or_init` reachable for the same key concurrently
threats.source: any party able to interleave requests in a threaded embedder
threats.title: Concurrent counter removal panics and poisons the shared mutex

threats.action: issue puts to keep the cache at capacity, so every subsequent insert runs the eviction path

existingControls.description: eviction is triggered by an explicit capacity check before insert, so memory does stay bounded — the bug over-evicts rather than under-evicts, which is why it fails safe for memory

gaps: inclusive range `for _ in 0..=n` evicts n+1 entries (kvstore/src/cache.rs:42)

`order` gains an entry on every put, including overwrites of an existing key, so the deque desynchronizes from `map` and eviction pops stale keys that no longer correspond to live entries (kvstore/src/cache.rs:28-29)
threats.impact: `evict_oldest(n)` iterates `0..=n`, removing n+1 entries, and `put` already asks for `overflow + 1`, so each capacity-triggered insert evicts two entries rather than one. A low-value attacker flushes other tenants' cached entries at roughly twice the intended rate, and the cache runs persistently below its configured capacity. Violates the 'only as many as necessary' bound in docs/SPEC.md:10-12
mitigations: remove any prior occurrence of the key from `order` before pushing, so the deque mirrors the map
threats.title: Eviction discards more entries than the bound requires

threats.action: pass a buffer shorter than four bytes, or an unaligned slice, hoping the raw-pointer read runs out of bounds or on a misaligned address

existingControls.description: length is checked against 4 with an early return before the pointer is formed, and `read_unaligned` is used so alignment is not a precondition — the stated SAFETY comment matches the code

threats.impact: would be an out-of-bounds read of process memory — but the length precondition is checked and the read is explicitly unaligned, so the block is sound as written. Recorded because it is the workspace's only `unsafe`, and any future change to the length check or the read width turns it into a memory-disclosure primitive
impactedAssets: host filesystem outside the store root
mitigations: replace the unsafe block with `u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[..4].try_into().ok()?)`, which is equivalent, panic-free, and removes the only unsafe code in the workspace
prerequisites: attacker-controlled or short byte buffer reaches `FileStore::magic`
threats.source: any party controlling the bytes passed to `magic`
threats.title: Unaligned pointer read on an attacker-supplied buffer
